extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents, and patent examiners in India (Controller General of Patents guidance)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and procedural criteria for filing, examining, and deciding patent applications under the Indian Patents Act and Rules, including substantive patentability standards and the examiner's checklist for formal and technical defects. Aimed at ensuring uniformity and homogeneity in processing patent applications in India.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements (three-part test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Therefore, the criteria for an invention to be patentable are, (1) An invention must be novel (2) has an inventive step and (3) is capable of industrial application
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory definition derived from S.2(1)(j) and supporting sections; all three criteria are cumulative and must be satisfied for grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty of the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel invention is one, which has not been disclosed, in the prior art where prior art means everything that has been published, presented or otherwise disclosed to the public on the date of patent... For an invention to be judged as novel, the disclosed information should not be available in the 'prior art'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed non-novelty examples/conditions: (a) anticipated by publication in any specification filed in India on or after 1 Jan 1912; (b) anticipated by publication in any document in any country before filing; (c) anticipated if claimed in any other complete specification filed earlier in India (even if published after); (d) anticipated by knowledge, oral or otherwise, in any local or indigenous community. Prior art includes disclosures in any language and any format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (non-obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventive step is a feature of an invention that involves technical advance as compared to existing knowledge or having economic significance or both, making the invention non obvious to a person skilled in the art. An invention shall not be considered as involving an inventive step, if, having regard to the state of the art, it is obvious to a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points: inventive step may include economic significance; judge by asking whether a non-inventive mind would have thought of the alleged invention; consider prior art in relevant field; combining teachings of documents is permissible if obvious to skilled person; assess invention as a whole (not merely parts); mere juxtaposition of known parts is likely obvious unless leading to synergistic effect; selection inventions should show surprising or unexpected technical solution; verifying previous predictions without advancement lacks inventive step. Examiner considerations listed: (a) scope and content of prior art; (b) assessing technical result/economic value; (c) differences between prior art and claimed invention; (d) defining technical problem; (e) final determination whether skilled person could bridge differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability (utility)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is capable of industrial application if it satisfies three conditions, cumulatively: (i) Can be made; (ii) Can be used in at least one field of activity; (iii) Can be reproduced with the same characteristics as many times as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility must be judged as of the date of filing; commercial or pecuniary success is not required; speculative or imaginary industrial uses do not satisfy requirement; the disclosure must enable the professed effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim or claims of a complete specification shall relate to a single invention, or to a group of inventions linked so as to form a single inventive concept (S.10(5)). All claims must refer to the same inventive idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable groupings include: product, process for its manufacture and use of the product; process and apparatus for carrying out the process; product, process for its manufacture and apparatus. Examples provided (spray bottle product, mechanism, process; gene sequence + uses/antibody/kit) illustrate linked claims. If claims define distinct inventions the application should be divided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure (complete specification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every complete specification shall (a) fully and particularly describe the invention and its operation or use and method by which it is to be performed; (b) disclose the best method of performing the invention which is known to the applicant and for which he is entitled to claim protection (S.10(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete specification must disclose enough for a person skilled in the art to perform the invention; include deposition details and source/geographical origin of biological material when mentioned. Non-disclosure of source/geographical origin is a formal and substantive defect flagged in examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and succinctness of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim or claims of a complete specification shall be clear and succinct and shall be fairly based on the matter disclosed in the specification (S.10(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate whether claims are clearly and properly worded; whether they are succinct (no unnecessary repetition, verbosity, excessive number, redundancy); whether claims sufficiently define the invention; whether claims are fairly based on and supported by the description and consistent with it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-patentable subject matter (Section 3 and 4 categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Various types of non-patentable inventions under Section 3: a) those which are not inventions (S.3) and b) inventions relating to atomic energy (S.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed subclauses include many exclusions (see separate rubric entries). The Manual also lists other excluded categories (computer program per se, mathematical methods, business methods, literary/dramatic works, presentations of information, etc.) and that section 4 excludes inventions related to atomic energy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 3(a): frivolous or contrary to natural laws
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention which is frivolous or which claims anything obvious contrary to well established natural laws is not patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: perpetual motion machines; merely making in one piece articles previously made in multiple pieces is frivolous. Mere usefulness alone is not sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 3(b): contrary to public order or morality; prejudice to life/health/environment
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention the primary or intended use or commercial exploitation of which could be contrary to public order or morality or which causes serious prejudice to human, animal or plant life or health or to the environment is not patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers inventions whose use is unlawful or injurious to public health (e.g., methods of adulterating food) or otherwise prejudicial; patenting such subject matter is excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 3(c): mere discovery of scientific principle or natural substance
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere discovery of a scientific principle or the formulation of an abstract theory or discovery of any living thing or non-living substances occurring in nature is not patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A scientific principle itself is not patentable, though using it in a process of manufacture that results in a substance or article may be patentable. Distinguish discovery (adds knowledge) from invention (suggests an act).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 3(d): mere discovery of new form/property/use of known substance
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere discovery of a new form of a known substance which does not result in enhancement of known efficacy or mere discovery of any new property or new use for a known substance or the mere use of a known process, machine or apparatus unless it results in a new product or employs at least one new reactant is not patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation lists salts, esters, polymorphs, isomers, etc., considered same substance unless differing significantly in efficacy. New use of known drug alone is not patentable; but a new method of preparing a substance may be. Examples and case law provided (aspirin, metric time device).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 3(e): mere admixture (aggregation of properties) not patentable
rubrics_metrics.description: A substance obtained by a mere admixture resulting only in the aggregation of the properties of the components or a process for producing such substance is not patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: simple mixture of sugar and colorants; combination of two known drugs with additive effects. Admixtures showing synergistic properties (soap, detergents, certain polymers) may be patentable. Examiner to check for unexpected or synergistic properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 3(f): mere arrangement/re-arrangement/duplication of known devices
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere arrangement or re-arrangement or duplication of known devices each functioning independently of one another in a known way is not patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mere juxtaposition of known integers that function independently is not patentable. If collocation produces working interrelation and new/improved results, subject matter may be patentable. Examples: umbrella with fan, bucket with torch, clock and transistor in one cabinet were held not patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 3(h): methods of agriculture or horticulture
rubrics_metrics.description: A method of agriculture or horticulture is not patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided where methods of cultivating/methods of producing plants/soil treatment were held not patentable. Generally processes of natural phenomena in agriculture/horticulture are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 3(i): methods of treatment of humans or animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Any process for the medicinal, surgical, curative, prophylactic, diagnostic, therapeutic or other treatment of human being or any similar process for animals is not patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therapeutic and prophylactic treatments, methods of curing illness, vaccinations and inoculations are considered therapy and excluded. Cosmetic applications may be treated differently if not therapy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software/computer program per se exclusion and technical contribution requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Computer programme per se is not patentable; inventions relating to application of computer program/software may be patentable when claimed in combination with hardware providing a 'technical advancement' over prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must describe the technical contribution and how hardware is controlled by software to overcome prior problems; technical character must be clearly shown in claims. Case law examples and reasoning (EPO/UK/US cases) are cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent application formalities and bibliographic data
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination sheet items: Kind of Application (NORMAL/PCT NATIONAL PHASE), Form of Application (Plain Paper/Form 1/Form 1A), Name, Nationality and Address of Applicant, Title, Provisional/Complete specification dates, Names and addresses of assignors/inventors, Endorsements, Death certificate & proof of title for deceased applicants, Date & Signature, Duplicate, Miscellaneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must verify that application form, applicant identity, inventorship, assignments and signatures are in order; missing or incorrect formalities may be flagged or require rectification.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT / National phase / Priority procedural checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Items include date of entry in national phase, international application number & country, date of earliest priority, entry within prescribed time, whether India designated/elected, international search report received, preliminary examination report received, certified copies, translations, authentication of translation, priority dates and countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must verify timeliness of national phase entry, priority filings within 12 months (convention applications), certified copies filed, translations and authentication for claims to priority or national phase entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement and Undertaking (Section 8, Rule 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prescribed form for Statement and Undertaking; name, address and nationality of applicant; petitioning for prior filings in foreign countries (pre- and post-filing disclosures); petitions for extension of time under section 8 and rule 138.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners check compliance with disclosure of foreign filings and timely furnishing of information per Section 8; non-compliance can affect examination and objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description: clarity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: DESCRIPTION - Clear: (a) Not in clear English; (b) English equivalent necessary in respect of [vernacular]; (c) Not clear in respect of where indicated; (d) Description in page inconsistent; (e) Distinguishing features as compared with prior art given is not clear; (f) Drawings to be separated from specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must ensure the description is clear and consistent; may require further description, revision, drawings or separation of drawings from specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description: sufficiency checks (further description/biological deposits)
rubrics_metrics.description: DESCRIPTION - sufficient: (a) Further description necessary; (b) Revision necessary where indicated; (c) Drawings required; (d) Biological materials - deposit in authorised depository institution, date/number of deposit and source/geographical origin in specification; (e) Model or sample required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For biological inventions, deposit details and source must be provided. Examiner flags need for additional experimental/theoretical detail or drawings to enable reproduction by skilled person.

rubrics_metrics.name: References and prior/pending application citations
rubrics_metrics.description: DESCRIPTION - references: replace references to foreign specifications by Indian equivalents or supplement; co-pending application numbers necessary; prior patent pages may be insufficient; distinguishing features with reference to prior specification necessary; acceptance may be deferred due to unpublished co-pending applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners require proper cross-references and adequate distinction from prior/pending applications; deficiencies may delay acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings: clarity and sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: DRAWINGS - clear: figures not numbered; sectional lines not marked; reference letters/numerals not marked; same reference letters used for different parts; part denoted in figure not same as in page; drawings do/do not clearly illustrate features. DRAWINGS - sufficient: arrangement described or claimed should be illustrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners check reproducibility, completeness (number of sheets, figures), that drawings support the description and claims; may require reproducible, correctly marked, and consistent drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims: clarity, succinctness, definitiveness, consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: CLAIMS - clear: claims not clear in expression or wording. CLAAMS - succinct: unnecessary repetition; verbose; large number; redundant. CLAIMS - definitive: claims do not sufficiently define the invention or are not sufficiently definitive. CLAIMS - consistent: claims not consistent with description, not supported by description, not fairly based on the matter disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must identify and object to unclear, verbose, over-broad, unsupported or inconsistent claims; indicate suggested amendments and grounds for objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title: appropriateness and precision
rubrics_metrics.description: TITLE - appropriate: inconsistent with description and claims. TITLE - precise: not precise, not clear in respect of word(s), vernacular words, does not sufficiently indicate the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner to request replacement or amendment to title to accurately and precisely reflect the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: ABSTRACT: Title; Concise summary; Size; Reference numerals of the Drawings; Searchable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract must be concise, include necessary reference numerals if appropriate, be of prescribed size and formatted/searchable for indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability and Pre-grant Opposition checklist (sufficient description and subject-matter grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections: (A) Sufficiency of description issues; (B) Subject matter objections including: does not constitute an 'invention' under Section 2(1)(j), inventive step/non-obviousness, industrial application, claims fall within Section 3 clauses (frivolous, contrary to public order/morality, prejudice to life/health/environment, mere discovery, mere new use, mere admixture, mere arrangement, method of agriculture, methods of treatment, plants/animals/essentially biological processes, computer programme per se, mathematical/business methods, literary/musical/aesthetic creations, mere scheme/rule/mental act/game, presentation of information, topography of integrated circuits, traditional knowledge aggregation). Also claims not allowable under Section 4; is not proper for patent of addition; statement of claims not definitive in view of what is admittedly known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an examiner's substantive checklist for patentability and pre-grant opposition issues; each listed ground must be considered and reasons recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty / anticipation checks in examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty: (a) Invention anticipated by (i) prior publication (ii) prior claiming; (b) Claim(s) conflict with claim(s) of [other applications]; (c) Invention claimed in claim(s) prima facie lacking in novelty; (d) Specification not clearly worded; (e) Consideration deferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must search and identify prior art that anticipates the claimed subject matter and raise objections or defer consideration where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single invention / plurality of inventions check
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims define a plurality of distinct inventions; each claim relates to an independent invention; claim(s) relate to an invention distinct from the rest; consider division if multiple inventions present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple discrete inventions are present, the examiner may require division of the application or additional fees; identify when claims are not linked by a single inventive concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity/date/earlier application check
rubrics_metrics.description: IDENTITY - date: Not allowable as an earlier application in respect of identical invention was filed in [earlier jurisdiction/date]. IDENTITY - Subject matter: does not constitute one invention or a group so as to make a single invention; application should be divided; cognate applications may require additional fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine priority/earlier filings and identity of subject matter to avoid double-patenting or improper claiming; enforce division where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requests and miscellaneous procedural actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for amending or correcting (application/specification/drawings), request for post-dating, request for postponement of acceptance, warning regarding time for putting the application in order of acceptance, specification and drawings generally unsatisfactory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must handle formal petitions, extensions, amendments, and issue warnings where time limits or substantive defects exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination sheet: checklist structure and categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The Examination Sheet enumerates items (numbered) covering bibliographic details, PCT/national phase matters, statement & undertaking, specification components, inventorship, drawings, claims, title, abstract, patentability grounds, novelty, unity, identity, and other formal and substantive checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This structured checklist is to be filled by examiners and used to ensure that all required checks (formal and substantive) are performed uniformly; entries include yes/no flags and spaces for dates/signatures and miscellaneous notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of technical contribution for software-related inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: When the invention involves software, the technical problem which needs to be solved by the invention should be sufficiently described as to how the hardware is controlled by the software to overcome the previously described problem. The 'technical character' of the invention should be brought out clearly in the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should determine whether the claimed combination of hardware and software yields a technical advancement over prior art; mere automation or business/mental acts performed by software are insufficient; case law examples underscore requirement for 'technical contribution'.
